parts.text:
2
What is not an SI base unit?
A
coulomb
B
kelvin
C
kilogram
D
second

hints: Notice the word not - three of the listed units are from the seven SI base units and one is built from other units.
Recall what kelvin, kilogram and second measure: temperature, mass and time are all base quantities in SI.
Recall that charge is linked to current and time by $Q = It$, so check whether the coulomb can be written as $\text{A s}$.
walkthrough: List the question choices: coulomb, kelvin, kilogram and second, and recall that SI has seven base units including those for mass, time, temperature and electric current.
Identify kelvin as the base unit for temperature, kilogram as the base unit for mass, and second as the base unit for time.
Recall the base unit for electric current is the ampere, not the coulomb.
Use $Q = It$ to show charge is derived: unit of $Q$ is the ampere multiplied by the second, so $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$.
Therefore the coulomb is a derived unit and is the one that is not a base unit. This is option A.

A.explanation: The coulomb is a derived unit for charge, since $Q = It$ gives $1 \text{ C} = 1 \text{ A s}$.

B.explanation: The kelvin is the SI base unit for thermodynamic temperature.

C.explanation: The kilogram is the SI base unit for mass.

D.explanation: The second is the SI base unit for time.
